question: Should WhatsApp require explicit bounded local roots for every injected media reader, accepting that reader-only integrations may stop sending local files after upgrade?
rationale: The branch closes an implicit host-file access widening but deliberately removes a working compatibility path, so automation cannot decide the security-versus-upgrade policy.

options.title: Require explicit roots
options.body: Keep the fail-closed boundary and require affected integrations to supply bounded local roots, with upgrade documentation and focused compatibility tests.

options.title: Provide a deprecation window
options.body: Temporarily retain a narrowly named reader-only compatibility path with warnings, tests, and a concrete removal release.

options.title: Narrow the PR
options.body: Land only strict base64 and canonical media refactoring while deferring the injected-reader boundary to a separately approved change.

recommendation.title: Require explicit roots
recommendation.body: Keep the fail-closed boundary and require affected integrations to supply bounded local roots, with upgrade documentation and focused compatibility tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They own this implementation and have prior merged history in the WhatsApp area, making them the best available person to clarify the intended boundary.
